newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Novo betters Q1 expectations.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Novo betters Q1 expectations.

text.p: Danish biotech group Novo Nordisk on Wednesday exceeded both its own and analysts' expectations when it announced first quarter 1997 profits slightly up on the same period last year.
Novo logged net profit of 398 million crowns on turnover of 3.6 billion, compared to last year's profit of 396 million and turnover of 3.4 billion.
Earnings per 10-crown share were also slightly up, at 5.30 crowns compared to 5.28.
Analysts had on average forecast profit of 393 million crowns and Novo itself repeatedly said it expected a fall.

Wednesday's accounts reported an overall increase in sales of seven percent and a 40 percent rise in income from licence fees and other operating revenues, mainly from licensing of its antidepressant Seroxat/Paxil.
Total costs rose seven percent, although direct production costs decreased.

Novo said that, measured in dollars, United States sales fell by six percent compared to the first quarter of 1996 due to a fall in the sale of insulin in vials and high first quarter 1996 distributor stockbuilding ahead of a price rise.
But the average value of invoicing currencies was about three percent higher in the first quarter of 1997 than the same period the year before, it added.
It retained its forecast for full-year 1997 pre-tax profits 15 percent higher than 1996's 2.5 billion crowns.
At 1100 GMT the group's share was three crowns up on Tuesday's close, at 687.00 crowns. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
